title: SSH Password Authentication Failure
detection_hypothesis: If credentials are guessed against the secure shell service, the authentication log will contain repeated password failure messages naming the target account and the source address.

field_semantics.ProcessName: Program name recorded by the system logger.
field_semantics.Message: Free-text message body recorded by the system logger.

collection_prerequisites: The authentication facility is forwarded from the host to the collector.
The syslog message body is preserved rather than truncated.
expected_collection_gaps: Hosts using journald without syslog forwarding require a different collector.
Rate-limited syslog can drop bursts of failures.
normalization_assumptions: ProcessName holds the syslog program name and Message holds the free-text body.
SourceIp is populated only for network authentication attempts.
ingestion_differences: Distribution-specific message wording differs between sshd builds.
Some pipelines pre-parse the message into structured fields.
retention_considerations: Authentication logs are low volume; 365 days of retention is common.
expected_volume: Moderate to high on internet-facing hosts.
false_positive_strategy: Single failures are almost always benign. Value comes from volume and spread, so route this rule to correlation rather than to an analyst queue.
tuning_guidance: Do not exclude individual users. Instead use the correlation rules that group by source address and count distinct target accounts.
test_strategy: Positive cases record password and key failures. Negative cases record a success, a session close, and a failure reported by a different daemon.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
